Encode the scaled attributes $s$ using a G-PCC attribute coder [S1].

The claim states that scaled attributes $s$ are encoded using a G-PCC attribute coder [S1]. The evidence in Source [S1] explicitly confirms this in multiple places: 1) The notes state 'Encode the scaled attributes s using G-PCC attribute coders based on RAHT or Predlift transforms'. 2) The passage states 'we encode our attributes s with both predictive coding schemes based on RAHT and Prediction and Lifting transforms (Predlift [13]), using quantization stepsizes in the bit-rate range expected from G-PCC’s common test conditions.' 3) The passage also mentions 'compressed with G-PCC methods'. Since the evidence confirms that the attributes are encoded using G-PCC standards (specifically via RAHT or Predlift transforms which are part of G-PCC), the claim is fully supported.

This maps the integer grid indices to a continuous coordinate space suitable for point cloud coding [S1, S2].

Both Source [S1] and Source [S2] explicitly describe a process where integer grid indices (xoct) are mapped to a continuous coordinate space (xpc) using the formula xpc = xoct × 2^M - 0.5. This mapping allows the PlenOctree nodes to be treated as a voxelized point cloud, which is then encoded using Geometry-based Point Cloud Coding (G-PCC) standards. This directly supports the claim that the evidence maps integer grid indices to a continuous coordinate space suitable for point cloud coding.

A variant that reduces bitrate by encoding only the colors (attributes) of non-occluded voxels for each viewpoint [S3].

The claim states that the variant reduces bitrate by encoding only the colors (attributes) of non-occluded voxels for each viewpoint. Source [S3] explicitly confirms this in the passages: 'This “Occlusion Aware” approach encodes for each color triplet of the PPC only the colors of the non-occluded voxels at each viewpoint k.' It further explains that the geometry is transmitted once losslessly, and only the attributes of the sub-point clouds (non-occluded points) are encoded, which leads to bitrate savings.
